findings.title: UTF-8 lead inside CSI delays the known syntax fault and lets a later byte-limit fault replace it
findings.contract: Frozen design sections 5/6: CSI has ASCII parameter/intermediate/final byte classes; the first syntax/resource fault is reported immediately once; resource priority applies only to faults on the same byte.
findings.command: source /workspace/work/validation/sdk/cangjie/envsetup.sh; cd /workspace/work/rich-text-review/probe; cjpm build; TERM=dumb COLORTERM= timeout 30s target/release/bin/main
findings.expected: First feed returns MalformedSequence at offset 0 when C2 arrives; later feed does not replace or duplicate this first fault. The C2 A0 scalar remains UTF-8 validated and the sequence drains to m.
findings.actual: First feed returns no diagnostics. Second feed returns SequenceTooLong at offset 0. For the same complete bytes with budget 4, the result becomes MalformedSequence at offset 0.
findings.impact: The externally visible first-fault kind and delivery timing violate the exact streaming error contract on a valid UTF-8 stream; a later resource failure suppresses the earlier syntax failure. No payload escape or terminal-control execution was observed.
findings.fix_boundary: Preserve byte-order framing diagnostics for a known-invalid lead within an existing CSI while continuing SDK UTF-8 validation, first-fault deduplication, draining, and permanent InvalidUtf8 failure semantics. Do not reinterpret continuations or change normal UTF-8 C1 recognition. Independent test author and product author own follow-up work.

nonblocking_limits: Existing final bundle boundary check exits 1 for missing examples/composition/cjpm.toml; benchmarks/rendering is also a later required release deliverable. This is retained as full-release incompleteness, not a new TASK009 blocker.
InputTooLarge near Int64.Max is assessed from the pre-increment guard and bounded counters; no infeasible exabyte runtime probe was attempted.
TASK083 independent test execution and TASK084 acceptance remain separate; this review does not close them or claim Linux release completion.
